lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: skills grow with practice

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 2 — earning and work
objective: Learners track an invented count of finished work across three weeks of practice, find the growth between weeks, and project a steady rate forward.
scenario: Ivy is a made-up third grader learning to fold napkins at a pretend family restaurant. In week one she folds 4 napkins in ten minutes, in week two she folds 7, and in week three she folds 9. These counts are invented to show what practice does.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compare Ivy's first week with her third week.

prompts.text: How many more napkins does Ivy fold in week three than in week one?

tasks.directions: Now look at all three of Ivy's practice weeks together, then check whether the second week was really an improvement on the first.

prompts.text: How many napkins does Ivy fold across all three weeks?
How does Ivy's week two compare with her week one?

tasks.directions: Suppose Ivy holds steady at her week-three speed of 9 napkins for the next four practice weeks.

prompts.text: How many napkins would Ivy fold across those four weeks?
How many more is that than her first three weeks put together?

tasks.directions: Ivy did not get faster by accident.

prompts.text: What does Ivy's week-by-week change show about what practice does to a skill someone gets paid for?

remediation: When a learner adds instead of comparing, write Ivy's three weekly counts on separate cards and slide the week-one card directly beneath the week-three card, so the question of how many more is answered by looking at the gap between two rows.
extension: Have the learner sketch what Ivy's fourth week might look like if practice keeps helping but she cannot fold faster than twelve, and explain the ceiling.
